messages.author: 94ee896ae0b97baf
messages.subject: measurement error in Lavaan
parts:
Hello all,  
I want to get some help with some error.
I ran a measurement model - This is my code.

SUMMERMODEL<-' risk =~a+b+c                                   

                                  MH =~d+e                                                  

                                  PH =~f+g '

fit2<-cfa(SUMMERMODEL, data = SUMMER_final, missing= "FIML")

summary(fit2, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)


It worked but I got this error.
Warning message: In lav_data_full (data=data, group=group, cluster=cluster, ; lavaan warning: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others ; use varTABLE(fit ) to investigate.

so I ran varTABLE(fit). THIS IS THE RESULT.

name idx nobs    type        exo user    mean       var        nlev  lnam
a       276  295  numeric     0      0        1.9           0.65
b       299  282   numeric    0      0        2.5           0.98
c       290   294  numeric    0      0        0.3           0.05
d       306   279   numeric   0      0       23.10     152.27
e      331    282   numeric    0     0       20.98     176.20
f       307    276   numeric    0     0        3.01         0.45
g      320    269   numeric    0     0        8.78         9.25

Just one note : a,b,c, f, g are means  and d, e are total scores. 
what should I do with this error ?

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: measurement error in Lavaan
parts:
Simplest thing is to divide d and e by 10 (and remember to re-scale when interpreting regression coefficients).

Having variables on vastly different scales like this can cause computational challenges.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: measurement error in Lavaan
parts: You're welcome! And yes, when you've run the structural model, you'll need to rescale coefficients involving d or e by either multiplying (when they're the outcome) or dividing (when they're the predictor) the structural parameter by 10 to be able to interpret them in their original scale.
